candidate.answerReason: The unique mode must be 6, forcing the mean to be 6 and the total to be 42. The six known numbers sum to 31, so x is 11; the resulting median is also 6.

methods.label: Use the unique mode first
methods.explanation:
The number \(6\) already occurs twice. Adding one value \(x\) can make another number occur at most twice, which would only tie \(6\). Therefore, if the mode is unique, it must be \(6\).

The mean must also be \(6\), so the seven numbers must total \(7\cdot6=42\). The six known numbers total \(31\), giving
\[
x=42-31=11.
\]
For this value, the ordered list is \(3,4,5,6,6,7,11\). Its fourth value, hence its median, is \(6\), and \(6\) is its unique mode. Thus all conditions hold, and \(\boxed{x=11}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).

review.mathematicalCheck: No value other than 6 can become the unique mode after adding just one observation. Thus the mean must be 6, forcing \(x=7\cdot6-31=11\). The resulting ordered list has median 6 and unique mode 6, establishing existence and uniqueness.
